nodes.label: BR-P4-003 Value-weighted blended risk
nodes.rationale: A single expensive line's violation can outweigh many cheap violations because deviation is weighted by order value share.

nodes.label: Fields hidden from CUSTOMER-role callers
nodes.rationale: Cost/margin/risk fields are omitted from the payload entirely, not just hidden in UI, so customer portal never receives deal cost or policy-deviation info.

nodes.label: Optimistic locking (expectedVersion)
nodes.rationale: Prevents silently overwriting a colleague's concurrent edit by failing with 409 VERSION_CONFLICT when the stale version is supplied.

nodes.label: Blended discount risk score formula
nodes.rationale: Combines worstLineExcessPct (catches one badly over-limit line that value-weighting would dilute) with orderExcessPct (catches many slightly-over-limit lines that individually look fine) so neither failure mode escapes detection.

nodes.label: Catalogue snapshots on line add
nodes.rationale: productName/sku/category/unitPrice/unitCost/taxRate are copied at add-time so a later product price change doesn't silently restate an existing quotation.

nodes.label: Discount governance (stricter of tier vs category limit)
nodes.norm_label: discount governance (stricter of tier vs category limit)
nodes.rationale: Nothing hardcoded; missing config defaults to 100% ceiling ('no policy') rather than 0%, since defaulting to 0 would flag every line on every order.

nodes.label: Last line absorbs rounding residue
nodes.rationale: Ensures sum of allocated discount shares equals the quotation discount amount exactly, avoiding a paisa/cent shortfall from naive equal division.

nodes.label: Over-limit discounts recorded, not rejected
nodes.rationale: Key Phase 3 decision: the literal spec wording would hard-reject over-limit discounts, but that is incompatible with the approval model where an over-limit discount is a legitimate request auto-routed for approval. Hard-rejecting would make the approval ladder unreachable.

nodes.label: Rounding policy: round-per-step, 2dp ROUND_HALF_UP
nodes.rationale: Rounding each value as it is produced (rather than rounding only at the end) keeps the returned document internally consistent — the shown numbers actually subtract/add to each other.

nodes.label: Layered architecture (domain layer testable without DB)
nodes.norm_label: layered architecture (domain layer testable without db)
nodes.rationale: Each layer knows only about the layer below it; the pure domain layer needs no DATABASE_URL/Postgres, which is why the 48 unit tests run in under a second on a clean checkout.

nodes.label: One transaction per command
nodes.rationale: Persisted lines and totals can never disagree; audit entry cannot survive a rolled-back change nor a change go unrecorded.

nodes.label: Unauthorised reads return 404 not 403
nodes.rationale: A 403 would confirm the id is real and leak which customers a rival rep is quoting; FORBIDDEN is reserved for cases where the caller can already see the resource.

nodes.label: Blended Discount Risk Score
nodes.rationale: Decides whether a quotation needs manager (and finance) approval by checking every order line against its own category-specific discount limit rather than one overall order limit, then computing a blended score across the whole order. This prevents a rep from keeping every individual line technically within limits while still discounting the overall order more than intended, and catches the case where many small per-line overages add up (each a little over its own limit) without any single line looking alarming alone. It exists so managers are not stuck reviewing every quotation by hand, only the risky ones.

nodes.label: Technical Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Teams may use any tech stack (language, framework, database) because the focus is business logic, data modeling, and workflow, not platform; core business rules (approval routing, discount governance, warehouse splitting, billing proration) must be implemented in real application logic, not hardcoded or faked for the demo; the customer facing negotiation screen must be a real, separate, restricted view; multi currency/multi company support is a bonus, not required.

nodes.label: Why This Hackathon Problem Is Important
nodes.norm_label: why this hackathon problem is important
nodes.rationale: Justifies the hackathon problem: mirrors a real B2B end-to-end sales workflow (Quotation -> Approval -> Fulfillment -> Billing -> Customer Negotiation -> Reporting), focuses teams on business logic (discount approvals, warehouse splitting, subscription billing, margin impact, customer negotiation) rather than UI polish, and pushes production-like system thinking with role-based access, approval chains, inventory coordination, recurring billing, audit trails, and deal analytics.

nodes.label: BR-P4-015 Data-driven discount limits & thresholds
nodes.rationale: Admin can change discount limits and thresholds via Phase 2 admin routes without redeploy; engine reads current values every invocation.

nodes.label: Data-Driven Proof step
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates that changing discount tier/category limits via admin API changes risk scoring immediately, proving nothing is hardcoded.
